title: A payer letter that writes a Social Security or phone number glued to another number (a currency amount's digits, four digits or more, an amount's cents or a date before its own shape; cents, a second number or a date after it; an amount's cents before a bare nine or ten), behind its label with the call's own identifier or the label's list number between them (on the next line too), masked and glued to a word, after a Social Security label glued to a word, or, in a letter whose digit chain only a range of two kinds holds, in a shape no pattern reads (amount-shaped, a five and four, a local number, beside the range)
assertion: No digit of it is sent: it is `[SSN]` or `[PHONE]`, or the letter is refused with `identifier_left`. A match ef3e8d20 did not make is applied only where the letter is not refused without it, and whatever is left as written is refused by the check (a property over labels, identifiers, list numbers and joined numbers, an invisible character among the joiners); a twin in its own shape with an amount, a date or a second number glued to it is never sent with four of its digits in a row (a property). References a noun names or no structure marks (`Case No. 123-45-678901`, `Referral # 123-45-67890-01`, `2026-0115-123-4567`), a row of long numbers and dates, masked account numbers, a number in parentheses that is no list number and what a held letter places by its structure (ZIP+4 after a state, a TIN, a code list, a service-line row) are sent unchanged. Every row of ruling A in `redact.residuals.json` (697) is refused or redacted, row by row
noFileReason: Letters are written in memory by the tests, a property among them, and the pinned rows are synthetic text in src/redact.residuals.json; no file.
